verdict.rationale: Aider can be scripted for unattended runs: `--message` executes one instruction, applies the edits and exits, and a Python `Coder.run()` API supports programmatic use. `--watch-files` mode monitors the repo and acts on `AI!` comments without chat interaction, and `--auto-test` runs tests after each edit. These are building blocks the user must wire up with external tooling (cron, CI, scripts). Aider has no first-party background automation system, and the autonomy mode mentioned by the community is a third-party add-on. Missing for 10: built-in scheduling/triggers or background job management, first-party autonomous multi-step agent mode, hosted/cloud background runs, independent hands-on corroboration of unattended automation.
